newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Maize farmers have told Land and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom that an amount of R200 million in levies paid last year to the maize board - due to be dismantled next month - should be returned to the farmers.

- Government red tape could see the motor industry fork out more than R100 million in additional duties to government this year after customs department lawyers delayed a planned reduction in tariffs, industry sources said.

- It was "ridiculous" that life assurance commissions were regulated by law, but payments to brokers for competing products such as unit trusts were not, Liberty Life vice-chairman Dorian Wharton-Hood said.

- Pan Africanist Congress (PAC) chairman and former president Clarence Makwetu, who was relieved of his parliamentary seat on Friday while he was visiting Kenya, said on Sunday he was not aware he was no longer an MP.
BUSINESS REPORT
-The Life Offices Association (LOA), the representative body for South Africa's insurance industry, could be under threat if Liberty Life refuses to back down in a dispute over brokers' commission.

- Nissan Motor Co Ltd of Japan will acquire a 50 percent stake in Automakers, the holding company of Nissan South Africa, for R3,90 a share, or a total of R360.75 million, effective from July 1 this year, Akio Sumitomo, a director of Nissan Motor of Japan, said on Friday.
- Trade in Inca bonds, or the more than one billion in corporate bonds issued last month by the Infrastructure Finance Corporation (Inca), officially started on Friday on the Bond Exchange.
- The government has appointed the British Overseas Development Administration as an adviser on the restructuring of South Africa's public service.
SAKE BEELD
- Sanlam has undertaken until the year 2000 to hold on to its 37 percent share in Automakers.
- Nissan Japan investment of R360 million in Automakers will be the biggest direct investment in South Africa.
THE STAR

- Parents of a 5-month-old baby girl were reunited with their child on Sunday, two days after she was kidnapped allegedly by her babysitter from their home near Bloemfontein in the Free State province.
- Residents in Johannesburg and Pretoria can expect at least another week of wet weather as rainfall averages continue to soar into record-breaking figures.
- A massive power cut left large sections of Johannesburg in the dark on Sunday after a fire caused extensive damage to a western Johannesburg substation.
